Consult Summary:
- Acute asthma flare with wheeze and exertional dyspnea in a patient with remote history of childhood asthma; plan to optimize inhaler use, obtain peak flow monitoring, and arrange follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing with shortness of breath for 2–3 days; fever and cough reported.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began 2–3 days ago and are ongoing; patient reports exertional dyspnea and difficulty finishing sentences; currently feels well at times.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors: Possible triggers include pollen or viral infection (asthma flare suspected).
- Associated symptoms: Cough; fever reported by patient; no sputum production; no blood in cough; no chest pain; no nocturnal symptoms.
- Respiratory history: History of asthma in childhood; considered quite bad then; required inhalers; sometimes hospitalized; not ICU; missed school occasionally; asthma meds stopped 3–4 years ago.
- Current baseline: Last years ago; uses salbutamol inhaler (noted as previously used regularly; exact dose/frequency not documented).
- Other medical history: Hay fever; eczema.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); regular antihistamines not currently used (per discussion, to be started later); other meds not reported.
- Social history: Non-smoker; drinks alcohol (one glass of wine) every 2–3 days; lives with partner; works as an engineer; currently teleworking or off sick in the last days.
- Family history: Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (childhood; historical severity described as quite bad; used inhalers; had hospital visits; not ICU; stopped medications ~3–4 years ago).
- Hay fever.
- Eczema.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Regular antihistamines (not currently used; planned inquiry/therapy noted).
- No other medications documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Smoking: No.
- Alcohol: One glass of wine, every 2–3 days.
- Living situation: Lives with partner.
- Occupation: Engineer; working from home recently; on sick leave at times.

Family History:
- Not provided.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Exam findings: Not provided.

Investigations:
- Peak flow meter and spacer to be prescribed; pharmacist to demonstrate use.
- Record peak flow values (morning and evening) after device is obtained.
- No laboratory or imaging results discussed.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute asthma flare (likely triggered by pollen or viral infection)
  - Plan:
    - Increase inhaled short-acting beta-agonist (salbutamol) use to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours.
    - Use spacer to improve inhaler delivery (spacer to be prescribed; spacer not currently owned).
    - Prescribe peak flow meter to monitor breathing; pharmacist to instruct use.
    - Record peak expiratory flow values on waking and in the evening for the next week.
    - If fever worsens or wheezing deteriorates, contact the clinic immediately for further guidance.
    - Schedule a follow-up review in about 1 week to assess control and consider additional medications if needed.

- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis/hay fever
  - Plan:
    - Recommend regular antihistamine (to be started; pharmacy guidance provided).
    - Document antihistamine plan in notes; patient to obtain from pharmacy.

- General Plan:
  - Educate on inhaler technique; pharmacist to demonstrate spacer use when device is picked up.
  - Reassess after peak flow monitoring and trial of intensified controller therapy if needed.
  - Advise patient to contact clinic with any escalation of symptoms or if unable to manage.

- Conflict noted:
  - Fever: Patient reports having a fever; later statements describe a temperature of 37°C and a claim that it was normal. Contradiction between “fever” report and temperature described as normal.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (BP, pulse, respiratory rate, temperature) not documented.
  - Comprehensive physical exam findings not documented.
  - Full medication reconciliation (doses/routes/frequencies) not documented for salbutamol.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Conflict noted regarding fever status (fever reported vs. temperature described as normal 37°C).
- Transcript quality:
  - Dialogue contains repetition and unclear timestamps regarding asthma history and current inhaler use; several details (exact inhaler type, dosing history) were not clearly documented in the transcript. No major inaccessible information detected beyond those inconsistencies.
